subject: Production chat stream slowdown — interim mitigations & customer follow-up
messages:
From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
To: samir.patel@atlascommerce.com, elena.gomez@atlascommerce.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-07T09:12:00Z
Subject: Production chat stream slowdown — quick mitigations we can apply now

Hi Samir / Elena,

Thanks for flagging the degraded streaming latency on your live chat sessions this morning. We saw a correlated increase in tail latency across a subset of streaming edge nodes between 08:40–09:05 UTC and wanted to get an interim set of mitigations to you while we investigate the root cause.

Quick steps you can try (no-code where possible):
- Switch to the non-streaming (polling) endpoint for high-concurrency flows: POST /v1/generate (this avoids the streaming I/O path).
- Reduce client-side max_tokens to 512 for now — normalizes token cadence and KV cache pressure.
- Enable client-side aggressive backoff on 503/504 and 429s: initial delay 200ms, exponential to 2s.
- If you control model selection, temporarily route to the slightly smaller variant (gptx-medium-1) which has similar quality but lower memory working set.
- Turn on our recommended prefix caching (prefix_cache=true) for commonly repeated system prompts — reduces repeated KV rebuilds.

Attachments: diag_stream_metrics_20270507.tar.gz (short capture), customer_timeline_AtlasCommerce.csv

We're deploying a prioritized patch to edge routing now; I'll update you with timelines in this thread. If you'd like, we can open a shared Zoom and walk through a live toggle.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192
From: samir.patel@atlascommerce.com
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: elena.gomez@atlascommerce.com, ops@atlascommerce.com
Date: 2027-05-07T09:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Production chat stream slowdown — quick mitigations we can apply now

Hi Vanessa — thanks for the fast response. Our SREs applied the non-streaming fallback for the highest-traffic rooms and saw immediate improvement in mean latency, but customers are still reporting occasional stalls when sessions spike.

Two asks:
1) Can Redwood confirm whether this is a routing/edge issue vs a model-side KV cache pressure problem? We need clarity for internal incident notes.
2) If this is a platform-side degradation, what compensation/credit process should we expect for the 3 hours of degraded UX in our main marketplace?

We can jump on a quick call; I'm available 10:30–11:30 PT.

Samir Patel
Director of Platform Engineering, AtlasCommerce
samir.patel@atlascommerce.com
From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
To: samir.patel@atlascommerce.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-07T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Production chat stream slowdown — quick mitigations we can apply now

Samir — appreciated. Short answers and next steps: 

1) Current signal (preliminary): the telemetry suggests a combination — a transient routing fan-in to a small subset of edge hosts plus an increase in long-context sessions that amplified KV cache churn. In plain terms: some requests were concentrated on an edge pool that then under-provisioned for concurrent KV working sets, which drove tail latency. We're still instrumenting to validate.

2) Compensation/credits: I've looped in Ben (sales lead) and Marissa (support/ops lead) to own the customer credit conversation and to confirm SLA calculations. We'll share a proposed credit and an incident summary by EOD tomorrow.

Immediate actions we've taken (and timeline):
- 10:00 UTC: Edge routing policy adjusted to redistribute new connects away from affected pool.
- 10:12 UTC: Autoscale thresholds temporarily lowered for streaming pools; extra capacity added.
- 10:20 UTC: Hotfix to our routing balancer to more evenly spread long-context sessions.
- Ongoing: Collecting full trace spans and KV cache stats (I attached a short capture).

We'll be in your 10:30 PT call — sending invite now.

—Vanessa
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: samir.patel@atlascommerce.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-09T16:45:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: Incident summary and next steps (AtlasCommerce)

Hi Samir / Elena — following our RCA session today, here's the agreed follow-up and what Redwood will deliver by next week: 

Summary (short):
- Impact window: 2027-05-07 08:40–11:20 UTC.
- Symptom: elevated tail latency and intermittent stalls on streaming/chat endpoints affecting a ~4% subset of sessions.
- Root cause (prelim): uneven routing to a small edge pool + increased KV cache churn from several long-context sessions.

Customer-facing remediation we executed:
- Immediate routing redistribution and autoscale adjustments (completed 10:20 UTC).
- Temporary recommendation to AtlasCommerce to use non-streaming fallback for surge flows (applied by the customer's SREs).

Planned next actions (deliverables):
- Engineering postmortem and timeline delivered by 2027-05-12.
- Model-serving change to reduce KV rebuild frequency for long-context sessions (deploy candidate 2027-05-14).
- Dedicated telemetry dashboard for AtlasCommerce showing percentiles and KV churn metrics (shared link by 2027-05-11).
- Proposed customer credit: 25% of streaming usage for the 3-hour window (Ben will confirm legal/finance ops).

Temporary mitigation checklist for your ops team (repeatable):
- Default to non-streaming generation for marketplace queues during peak traffic.
- Implement client-side token cap (512) and prefix caching for repeated system prompts.
- Use exponential retry with jitter; avoid immediate reconnect floods during incidents.

Attachments: incident timeline and sample traces (diag_stream_metrics_20270507.tar.gz).

We take this seriously and will include an action plan to prevent recurrence. Ben will reach out on the credits/contract implications; I'll follow up on the engineering timeline.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
